start_here: Say to your AI: "Show one person's answers to a form across every time they answered, in order, and the trend of one numeric answer, from the answer facts in the database", with {"form_id":"sample-intake","respondent_id":"respondent-1","field_map":{"budget":"budget"}}. It runs tool:read-answer-progress and answers {"rows":[{"id":"session-1","label":"2026-06-26T00:00:00Z","fields":{"budget":2000,"answeredAt":"2026-06-26T00:00:00Z"}}],"trend":{"field":"budget","points":[2000]},"latest":{"budget":2000,"answeredAt":"2026-06-26T00:00:00Z"},"count":1}
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it keeps its rows in tables of your own database, reached only on the local port your computer reports as own-rows-postgres.
instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Show one person's answers to a form across every time they answered, in order, and the trend of one numeric answer, from the answer facts in the database", and give it form_id; respondent_id; field_map (the name you want for each answer, to its questionId).
2. The AI calls run_resource_operation at @tools with method tools:run, tool tool:read-answer-progress and its input (the worked example shows one).

3. Read what comes back: Returns one row per time answered, oldest first, with the mapped answers and when; the numeric series for the trend; the latest row; and the count. A person who has not answered gets no rows.
4. It keeps its rows in tables of your own database, reached only on the local port your computer reports as own-rows-postgres.
